name: Pane
text: Pane: A one-click toggle between extremes still assumes users will switch—most won’t. The real risk is that dark mode becomes a placebo: users in bright rooms keep glare, users in dark rooms miss errors. Settle it with forced A/B exposure: show each user both modes for a week, then measure error detection speed and glare complaints. If dark mode wins, keep it; if not, default to high-contrast light with *subtle* dark accents for low-light users.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Force a one-week A/B exposure where every user sees both high-contrast light and dark modes, then measure error detection speed and glare comfort to pick the default.

Result: A single default theme (light or dark) with a one-click toggle, proven by data to balance error visibility and user comfort.
